sources.entry: Luanti - Voxel game engine (formerly Minetest). Play one of our many games, mod a game to your liking, make your own game, or play on a multiplayer server. (Source Code) LGPL-2.1/MIT/Zlib C++/Lua/deb

summary.one_liner: Luanti (formerly Minetest) is a free, open-source voxel game engine for playing, modding, and creating block-based games, including multiplayer servers.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Luanti as a voxel game engine with easy modding and game creation. It lists default controls for movement, building, digging, inventory, chat, fly/fast/noclip modes, camera, minimap, and debug screens. It documents where user data, worlds, and config files live on Windows, Linux, and macOS, and points to the configuration file (minetest.conf) and command-line options (--help). It also links to compiling guides for GNU/Linux, Windows, and macOS, plus Docker guides for developing and running a server. The README uses a major.minor.patch version scheme.
use_cases: run a dedicated server in Docker
build and compile the engine from source
how_to_run: Compile from source following the GNU/Linux, Windows, or macOS compiling guides linked in the README
Run a server with Docker using the linked Docker guide
Edit user/minetest.conf (created on first close) to configure the game
Run with --help to list command-line options
notable: Formerly Minetest, with the engine supporting Lua-based mods and game creation
Supports single-player and multiplayer server play
Documented per-platform paths for bin, share, and user data, with a MINETEST_USER_PATH override
caveats: The README does not describe installation steps beyond compiling from source or using Docker; prebuilt install paths are only referenced by location
Some documentation sections are only linked, not summarized in the README itself
